drawings.description: à droite, une figure : un cercle portant les points $\zeta_{-1}$, $\zeta_0$, $\zeta_1$, $\zeta_2$, $\zeta_3$, et plus haut à gauche $\zeta_{n-2}$ ; des flèches vont de $\zeta_{-1}$ à $\zeta_0$ (épaisse), de $\zeta_0$ à $\zeta_1$ ($e_1$), de $\zeta_1$ à $\zeta_2$ ($e_2$), de $\zeta_2$ à $\zeta_3$ ($e_3$), côtés successifs d'un polygone régulier inscrit, et une flèche épaisse marquée $\alpha$ va de $\zeta_0$ à $\zeta_3$.
drawings.kind: regular polygon inscribed in a circle, with side vectors and a diagonal
drawings.notes: A circle of which he draws the arc from the right, over the top, round the left to the bottom left; the lower right part, where the polygon lies, is not closed, and it is left open here. Five consecutive vertices zeta_{-1}, zeta_0, zeta_1, zeta_2, zeta_3 are computed on the circle at equal angular steps (37 degrees, fitted to the page); arrows along the four sides, the first heavy, the others labelled e_1, e_2, e_3; a heavy arrow alpha from zeta_0 to zeta_3; the label zeta_{n-2} beside the upper left of the circle, with no point. Question settled by the mathematics: the text says u is the rotation sending zeta_i to zeta_{i+1} and e_1, e_2, e_3 are successive sides, so the vertices are equally spaced on the circle; on the page the freehand vertices zeta_0 and zeta_1 fall inside the circle and the steps are unequal. Still differs: positions are regularised (up to 5 units from the freehand points); a second small arrow head half-way along the arrow alpha and a tick under e_1 are left out. Nothing struck; the foot of the half-sheet is torn below the figure. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.
